hero.lead: An island nation of 403,000 people, where visitors earned six tenths of export income in 2020 and a 2024 debt conversion refinanced $300 million to fund the protection of the sea.

capital.heading: Debt turned into an ocean fund.

register.name: International bond, 11 years, 2025
register.detail: Government of The Bahamas · priced June 2025 · coupon and re-offer yield 8.250% · 11-year maturity · 3.9 times oversubscribed
register.note: Funded the repurchase of $767 million of outstanding Eurobonds
register.text: A US dollar bond of 11 years sold to more than 60 investor accounts in North America, Europe and the Middle East at a coupon of 8.250%. It funded the repurchase of $767 million of outstanding Eurobonds and reduced principal repayments by $451 million over the next three years, with a portion for national development priorities, including infrastructure: the public finances behind all seven standards.

register.name: Climate Resilience of the Water Sector in The Bahamas (FP298)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved 28 March 2026 · GCF grant $37.506M and concessional loan $12.546M · CDB loan $12.546M · total $65.2M
register.note: Accredited entity: the Caribbean Development Bank, with the Water and Sewerage Corporation
register.text: Green Climate Fund finance, through the Caribbean Development Bank, for climate-resilient wellfields, pumping stations, storage and water-loss reduction on six islands, where water supply is at risk from storm surges, hurricanes and flooding. Desalination accounts for 81 per cent of the water produced; the project serves the water standard.

register.name: Climate Resilient Transport Infrastructure in New Providence
register.detail: IDB · approved December 2025 · 25-year term · 5.5-year grace period · interest based on SOFR
register.note: Over 296,000 residents of New Providence to gain better mobility in bad weather
register.text: An IDB loan for a programme of works on New Providence that upgrades drainage, builds flood-mitigation and stormwater infrastructure and improves road maintenance on the main corridors and residential roads, to reduce the disruption caused by recurring floods. It protects homes and the roads to work, school and clinics: the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Support the improvement of the electricity service in The Bahamas (BH-L1057)
register.detail: IDB · approved 22 October 2025 · signed at a ceremony on 20 November 2025 · second loan under a 2020 credit line for the energy sector · 25 years
register.note: Digitalisation and modernisation $81.9 million, institutional capacity $3.7 million, administration $4.4 million
register.text: An IDB loan for Bahamas Power and Light: smart meters installed at no cost to users, with a prepayment option, a SCADA system to manage the grids of the Family Islands, a map of the grid and stronger management. It serves the energy standard through more reliable and efficient electricity.

register.name: Disaster risk management programme, second loan
register.detail: IDB · second of a two-loan series · IDB release of 1 October 2025 · 20-year term · 5.5-year grace period
register.note: Follows the first loan of the series, also $160 million, approved in 2023
register.text: IDB support for the Bahamas to adopt the instruments created by its Disaster Risk Management Act: national humanitarian assistance standards, a disaster financing strategy, reference parameters for disaster management and an information system built on past disasters and projected scenarios. It protects the public finances behind all seven standards when hurricanes strike.

register.name: Local Sustainable Development in the Blue Economy (BH-O0011)
register.detail: IDB · credit line approved 3 April 2024 · first loan of $30 million signed 19 August 2025 · 25-year term · 5.5-year grace period
register.note: First loan: $17.7 million for small businesses, $5.1 million for BAMSI, $4.8 million for climate action
register.text: A ten-year IDB credit line for the Family Islands, with finance and technical help for about 120 small businesses in sustainable tourism, aquaculture and mariculture, marine and agricultural science at the Bahamas Agriculture and Marine Science Institute, and the management of marine protected areas. It serves the livelihood and food standards beyond New Providence and Grand Bahama.

register.name: Energy sector reform loan
register.detail: CAF · approved 29 June 2025 · first sovereign loan to the Bahamas since it joined CAF in November 2024
register.note: In support of the National Energy Policy
register.text: A CAF loan in support of the National Energy Policy: a modernised and digitised grid, more renewable energy, more affordable power and stronger energy institutions, with better access, efficiency and climate resilience for vulnerable island communities. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Disaster risk management programme, first loan
register.detail: IDB · first of a two-loan series · approved April 2023 · 20-year term · 5.5-year grace period
register.note: Supports the Disaster Risk Management Act, passed by Parliament in December 2022
register.text: IDB support for policy reforms that strengthen natural disaster risk governance: risk identification and reduction, disaster preparedness, recovery and financial protection. It protects the public finances behind all seven standards when hurricanes strike.

register.name: Sygnus Bahamas SME Receivables Working Capital (15286-01)
register.detail: IDB Invest · approved 15 July 2025 · signed 2 June 2026 · revolving line, available for up to five years
register.note: Guaranteed by Sygnus Credit Investments; announced by IDB Invest on 27 May 2026
register.text: A working capital line of up to $10 million from IDB Invest to Sygnus Investment Bahamas to grow its financing of receivables, so that local small and medium-sized enterprises are paid sooner for what their clients owe. It serves the livelihood standard through the firms that employ Bahamians.

register.name: Debt Conversion for Marine Conservation
register.detail: Standard Chartered loan · IDB guarantee $200M · Builders Vision co-guarantee $70M · AXA XL credit insurance $30M · 22 November 2024
register.note: IDB guarantee: $200 million; conservation funding managed by the Bahamas Protected Areas Fund
register.text: Refinanced $300 million of external commercial debt with a new loan from Standard Chartered, backed by guarantees and insurance. The savings, an estimated $124 million over 15 years, fund marine conservation, with an endowment expected to reach $20 million by 2039; it protects the sea that sustains Bahamian livelihoods.

items.name: Agricultural Development Organization
items.text: Opened the Centreville Community Farm on Fritz Lane on 21 May 2026 for residents facing food insecurity, the fifth of a plan for community farms in all 41 constituencies. About 70 percent of the produce goes to residents in need and 30 percent is sold to restaurants to sustain the farm.

items.name: Centre for Training and Innovation (One Eleuthera Foundation)
items.text: The first and only post-secondary, non-profit education and training institution and social enterprise on Eleuthera. Its student training campus in Rock Sound runs a 16-room training hotel, a restaurant and a farm.
